title: Prayer shawl in shell lace
subtitle: A top-down triangle with alternating shell rows and chain-space rows in DK cotton
excerpt: This triangular prayer shawl works from the top centre to a 160 cm width and 70 cm depth. Rows of five-treble shells alternate with rows of chain spaces to create a light, openwork fabric. The construction follows the traditional prayer shawl pattern of increasing every row. DK weight on a 4 mm hook gives a fabric that is firm enough to hold its shape but open enough to drape softly.
sourceNotes: Traditional prayer shawl pattern based on widely circulated community crochet designs, first documented in congregational needlework guides during the late 20th century. Shell-and-chain-space lace construction adapted from Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), chapter on crochet open work.

glossaryTerms.definition: Five trebles worked into the same stitch or chain space, creating a fan-shaped group. In this pattern shells sit above chain spaces on alternate rows.
A loop of chains spanning between two stitches or groups, left open so the following row can work into it. In this pattern ch-2 spaces sit between shells and anchor the row structure.

content.text: This prayer shawl grows from a short foundation chain at the neck down to a full triangular shape using alternating rows of five-treble shells and chain spaces. The structure is consistent throughout: odd rows place shells, even rows connect them with double crochet and chain arches. The shawl reaches 160 cm wide and 70 cm deep before a final shell border finishes all three edges.

attrs.title: Materials
attrs.body: Approximately 400 g DK-weight yarn. A 4 mm crochet hook (US G/6). Tapestry needle. Craft scissors. Stitch marker. Blocking mat and pins. Tape measure.

content.text: Gauge

One shell repeat (5 tr, ch 2) = approximately 3.8 cm wide; 12 rows = 10 cm deep in DK yarn with a 4 mm hook. This pattern uses shell-repeat count rather than stitch count to check gauge: at the first count row (Row 7) you should have 5 full shells across the row and the work should measure roughly 19 cm wide.
Stitches used
chain (ch): UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st): UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc): UK; the same move as US "single crochet" (sc).
treble (tr): UK; the same move as US "double crochet" (dc).
shell: 5 tr into the same stitch or chain space.
Pattern
The shawl is worked flat, turning at the end of each row. Shell rows and arch rows alternate throughout. On every shell row, an extra half-shell is added at each edge to build the triangle.
Foundation
Ch 6. Sl st to form a ring.
Row 1 (right side)
Ch 4 (counts as tr + ch 1). 2 tr in ring. Ch 2. 2 tr in ring. Ch 1. 1 tr in ring. Turn. (7 sts including ch)
Row 2 (arch row)
Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). 1 dc in first tr. Ch 2. 1 dc in ch-2 space. Ch 2. 1 dc in top of turning ch. Turn. (3 dc, 2 ch-2 arches)
Row 3 (shell row)
Ch 3 (counts as first tr). 2 tr in first dc. Ch 2. 5 tr in next dc (shell). Ch 2. 3 tr in last dc. Turn. (1 half-shell each end, 1 full shell at centre, 4 ch-2 spaces)
Row 4 (arch row)

Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). 1 dc in first tr. *Ch 2. 1 dc in next ch-2 space*; repeat from * to * across, ending 1 dc in top of turning ch. Turn. (count of dc = number of ch-2 spaces plus 2 edge dc)
Row 5 (shell row)
Ch 3 (counts as first tr). 2 tr in first dc. *Ch 2. 5 tr in next dc (shell)*; repeat from * to * across to last dc. Ch 2. 3 tr in last dc. Turn. (one extra shell added at each edge)
Rows 6 to approximately 84

Continue alternating Row 4 (arch row) and Row 5 (shell row). Each shell row adds one full shell to the row, growing the triangle by one shell repeat on each side. After approximately 42 shell rows (84 total rows), the widest row will contain approximately 42 shells and measure 160 cm. The depth will be approximately 70 cm.
Final edging

After the final arch row, work one round of shells around all three edges: join yarn at the top right corner, *sk 2 sts, 5 tr in next st, sk 2 sts, 1 sl st in next st*; repeat from * to * along the lower two diagonal edges. At the bottom point work (5 tr, ch 2, 5 tr) into the tip stitch to turn the corner. Do not shell along the straight top edge; instead work 1 dc in each stitch or chain along the top. Fasten off.
Finishing

Fasten off and weave in all ends securely. Wet-block by soaking in cool water for 10 minutes, then pressing out moisture gently and pinning to the finished dimensions on a blocking mat. Pin the bottom point first, then the two top corners, then ease the diagonal edges to shape at regular intervals. Leave until completely dry.
Care
Handwash in cool water with a mild detergent. Lay flat to dry. Do not tumble-dry or wring. Wet lace fabric is fragile: support the whole piece when lifting it from the water.
What to try next

Work the same shell construction in a sport-weight yarn on a 3.5 mm hook for a finer, lighter result. A contrast-colour shell border in a second shade gives a defined edge. To widen the shell, try 7 tr per shell instead of 5 and space the shells further apart with ch-3 arches between them.
